title: Marine Engineering Officer
raw_text:
8-881A. Military Occupational Specialty 881A--Marine Engineering Officer
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. AR 56-9. Must meet the academic and vessel-specific
requirements of U.S. Army Marine License annotated: "Chief Engineer of Class A-1 Motor
Vessels; Assistant Engineer of Class A-2 Unlimited Motor Vessels."
   b. Prerequisites. AR 56-9 and DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 881A. MOS 881A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are 21P and 88L
with ASI S2.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 1--Marine Deck Officer.
        (3) 2--Marine Engineering Officer.
        (4) 8--Instructor.
        (5) P--Parachutist.
        (6) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (7) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI.
        (1) 2B--Air Assault (personnel only).
        (2) 3R--Force Management.
        (3) 5W--Jumpmaster (personnel only).
        (4) 6M--Mobilization and Demobilization Operations.
        (5) 6P--Master Fitness Trainer.
        (6) 6T--Military Auditor (Reserve Component personnel only).
        (7) 7Q--Training Development.
   f. Qualifications. Marine Engineering Officer
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course.
              (b) Be certified and licensed at the 881A skill level, per AR 56-9.
              (c) Have a physical profile of not less than 222221, per AR 40-501.
              (d) Have a distance visual acuity, which corrects to at least 20/20 in one eye, and
20/40 in the other eye.
              (e) Have normal color vision based on no more than four errors in reading the pseudo
isochromatic plates test.
              (f) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security clearance of SECRET.
              (g) After four years of Marine Engineering Officer service, complete the Marine
Engineering Officer A2 Course for SQI 2 certification.
              (h) Be certified at the 881A2 skill level, per AR 56-9.
              (i) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power
Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036
shuttles.
       (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) Complete the Marine Engineering Officer Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
       (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
       (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
   g. Duties.
       (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Directs the operation, maintenance, repair, and overhaul of engineering
machinery and equipment installed aboard Army watercraft.
              (b) Supervises and performs installation and repair of marine power plant, propulsion
systems, heating and ventilation systems, and other mechanical plumbing and electrical
equipment in ships and marine facilities.
               (c) Inspects ship's machinery to determine compliance with maintenance standards
and/or to determine extent and nature of repairs required.
              (d) Maintains maintenance logbooks and prepares maintenance reports and work
orders.
              (e) Implements the Army Maintenance Management System (TAMMS) as it applies
to Marine material.
         (2) CW3--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Is responsible for the safe, efficient operation and maintenance of all engineering
systems aboard unlimited ocean transiting vessels.
              (c) Initiates and coordinates all Marine engineering and maintenance functions
associated with port operations at battalion level.
              (d) Conducts technical inspections and Marine condition surveys.
              (e) Provides technical guidance and direction in regard to Marine-related issues at
battalion level staff.
         (3) CW4--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
              (b) Coordinates all Marine engineering and maintenance functions associated with
port operations above battalion level.
              (c) Manages maintenance and repair activities.
         (4) CW5--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(3).
              (b) Performs as technical or Functional Systems Integrator at senior staff level.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) Table 8-881A-1. Physical requirements.
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-881A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-881A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
